A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same H-SPLID study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, Appendices A-G, and checklist support reliable comparison after matching relocated content.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification and robustness experiments, transfer evaluations, loss ablations, runtime measurements, and hyperparameter sensitivity results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Figure 1, Tables 2-5, and Appendix G.

M1.justification: The latent decomposition, loss components, alternating optimization, mask updates, and inference procedure are unchanged. Correcting L_ST to L and the sample index in Eq. (6b) resolves notation inconsistencies without establishing a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use C-MNIST, the four-class COCO subset, ISIC-2017, ImageNet-1K training, ImageNet-9 variants, and CounterAnimal splits. The evaluated attacks, corruptions, and background scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain vanilla training, weight decay, L1 regularization of weights and activations, Group Lasso regularization of weights and activations, and HBaR. No comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix F retain the same splits, architectures, preprocessing, training budgets, tuning procedures, metrics, and attack settings, including ten-step PGD with step size 0.0156.

E4.justification: The loss-component ablation in Table 5 and the runtime, hyperparameter sensitivity, and learning-rate analyses in Appendix G are unchanged. Their questions, configurations, and evidence are retained.

E5.justification: Reported repetition counts and uncertainty practices are unchanged, including five attack seeds, ten ISIC seeds, and single-seed ImageNet experiments. Neither version adds significance tests.

E6.justification: The empirical values and findings match, including appendix results. For example, both report H-SPLID accuracy of 57.5% under COCO background PGD at epsilon 3/255 and 60.6% on CA-Counter in Tables 2 and 4.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.2 changes from a perturbation vector delta to uniformly bounded input-dependent maps delta(x). Appendix C explicitly introduces a measurable perturbation map and expands the pointwise Taylor and norm inequalities in Eqs. (32)-(39). This is a targeted extension of the existing argument; the bound, kernel assumptions, supporting lemmas, and corollary remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about salient/non-salient decomposition, HSIC-and-dimensionality robustness bounds, and reduced reliance on irrelevant features. The revised theorem formulation does not change these headline claims.

C2.justification: The interpretations of robustness, transfer, and sensitivity results are retained, as are the limitations concerning contextual diversity, inseparable co-occurring features, and image-only evaluation. The theorem discussion adopts delta(x) without introducing a new mechanism explanation.

D1.justification: Implementation, hardware, hyperparameter, runtime, and data-access information remain unchanged. Although v2 removes the code link from the abstract, Section 4 retains the same repository and public-availability statement.

R1.justification: The references and related-work discussion match. Positioning relative to contrastive analysis, feature selection, and Wang et al.'s HSIC robustness work is unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 removes the duplicate abstract code disclosure, standardizes the loss notation, corrects the sample index, and revises the theorem and proof prose. The overall section structure and most wording remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Existing displays are redistributed: Table 2 moves from page 9 to page 8, Figure 4 from page 25 to page 26, and Tables 13-17 spread across pages 29-30. Figures, table structures, and captions are retained without new displays.

improvement.justification: v2 makes input-dependent perturbations explicit, exposes intermediate proof steps, and corrects indexing and loss-notation inconsistencies, modestly improving precision and auditability. The theoretical gain remains limited: both versions leave unjustified the transition from Eq. (31)'s absolute expected derivatives to an expected Jacobian-norm bound, used in v2 Eq. (39). The method and empirical evidence are unchanged.
